chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Maxwell's ethnic chameleon identity
summary: People mistake Maxwell's ethnicity; Clark Terry says he is the only white guy he's comfortable with.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You know, I've had a funny experience all my life. I said sometimes to my wife, you know, I don't

really know what, ethnically, I am. But I've had Italians say, you act like you're Italian, or I was in the Soviet Union, "Are you sure you're not Russian?" And I said about the only people who ask me if I'm sure I'm not, is black people, and on the other hand a guy like Clark says, "you're the only white guy I've ever been comfortable around. So I'm about as close as you can get.
I don't know whether I'm a chameleon or what I am.

You're a chameleon soul. Like you came in here the other day, walking through the kitchen, and my wife had some cornbread up there, and you jumped right in just like you were a brother and really enjoyed a slice of it.
Well, I grew up on that stuff. That was good, though.
We weren't going to offer any to you because we didn't want to scratch your throat.
What do you think we ought to talk about now? Let's hold it a while.
